record.paper_title: Space and Time Complexity of Exact Algorithms: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: For 10-CLIQUE, where the input is an undirected simple loopless p-vertex graph G and the task is to decide whether G contains a clique on 10 vertices, is there an algorithm running in O(p^7.5) time?

evidence.quote: Is there an O(p7.5) time algorithm for 10-CLIQUE?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E) be an undirected simple loopless graph on p = |V| vertices (no self-loops, no multiple edges). A clique on 10 vertices in G is a subset S ⊆ V with |S| = 10 such that every pair of distinct vertices in S is joined by an edge of G. The 10-CLIQUE decision problem asks, given such a graph G as input, to decide whether G contains a clique on 10 vertices.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that solves the 10-CLIQUE decision problem in time O(p^{7.5}) on the standard word-RAM model (uniformly in G), where p denotes the number of vertices of the input graph?
artifact.status_search_result: The fastest known k-clique algorithms use the Nešetřil–Poljak reduction to (rectangular) matrix multiplication, giving running time O(n^{ωk/3}) when 3 | k, and improvements due to Eisenbrand–Grandoni when k ≢ 0 (mod 3). For k = 10, the current best published bounds rely on the matrix multiplication exponent ω ≈ 2.371, yielding running times above n^{7.9}, well above n^{7.5}. No published algorithm achieves O(p^{7.5}) for 10-CLIQUE, and the question of attaining such a bound appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Algorithms for Clique Problems (Vassilevska)
status_evidence.snippet: The asymptotically fastest algorithm for k-clique runs in time O(n^{ωk/3}); only matrix multiplication based techniques beat trivial O(n^k).
status_evidence.claim: Best known k-clique runtimes derive from matrix multiplication, giving O(n^{ωk/3}) for k divisible by 3.

status_evidence.title: Faster Combinatorial k-Clique Algorithms (arXiv:2401.13502)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies improved combinatorial k-clique algorithms; algebraic bounds remain governed by ω.
status_evidence.claim: No improvement to O(p^{7.5}) for k=10 has been reported in the recent literature.
